title: Faith Makes for Stronger, More Lasting Marriages | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Short Daily Signal teaser (via IFS) on an IFS study finding that seriously practicing Christian couples report happier, more stable marriages; no figures given.

insights.claim: The Institute for Family Studies' September 2026 study 'The Devout Difference: Religion, Marital Quality and Sex Among Americans' tests whether faith leads to happier and more stable marriages, measuring marital happiness and confidence that the marriage will last.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Identifies the study and its two outcome measures; the article itself is only a teaser.
insights.locator: The Institute for Family Studies released the findings

insights.claim: Per the Daily Signal write-up, Christian couples who take their faith seriously are much more likely to remain married and report more joyful and meaningful marriages.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Religious seriousness is presented as a marriage-stability correlate; no numbers are given in this excerpt.
insights.locator: Christian couples who take their faith seriously are much more likely to remain married
